title: Middle Car
statement: A train is stored as a linked chain of cars. Car i is coupled to car next[i] behind it, or to nothing when next[i] is -1, and the locomotive pulls car head first. The chain visits every car exactly once. Return the index of the middle car: for an odd number of cars the exact middle, and for an even number the second of the two middle cars. Try to do it in one pass with constant extra memory.
constraints: Following next from head visits every car exactly once and ends at -1

examples.explanation: The order is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4; the middle car is 2.
The order is 1, 3, 2, 0. With four cars the second middle is car 2.

hints.content: Counting the cars first and then walking half way works in two passes.
Can one pointer tell you when another pointer has reached the middle?
Move one pointer one car at a time and another two cars at a time.
When the fast pointer runs out of cars, the slow pointer has covered half the distance.
Stop when fast is -1 or the car after fast is -1. That stopping rule gives the second middle for even lengths.

testCases.explanation: The order is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4; the middle car is 2.
The order is 1, 3, 2, 0. With four cars the second middle is car 2.
A single car is its own middle.
Seven cars in index order: the middle is 3.

solutions.title: Copy the order into an array
solutions.intuition: Once the cars are listed in order, the middle is just an index.
solutions.approach: Follow next from head, appending each car. Return order[floor(length / 2)].
solutions.pseudocode:
order = []; node = head; while node != -1: order.push(node); node = next[node]
return order[len / 2 floored]
commonMistakes: Using (length - 1) / 2, which picks the first middle for even lengths.
Returning the middle position in the array instead of the car index stored there.
solutions.interviewExplanation: Materializing the chain into an array makes the middle an index lookup. It's linear time but uses linear extra memory.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: For next [-1,3,0,2] and head 1, the order is [1,3,2,0].

solutions.title: Slow and fast pointers
solutions.intuition: A pointer moving twice as fast reaches the end exactly when the slow one is at the middle.
solutions.approach: Start slow and fast at head. While fast is not -1 and next[fast] is not -1, move slow one step and fast two steps. Return slow.
solutions.pseudocode:
slow = fast = head
while fast != -1 and next[fast] != -1: slow = next[slow]; fast = next[next[fast]]
return slow
commonMistakes: Reading next[-1] by advancing fast without checking it first.
Starting fast one step ahead, which returns the first middle instead of the second.
solutions.interviewExplanation: I move one pointer one car at a time and the other two at a time. When the fast one hits the end, the slow one has made half as many moves and sits in the middle. The loop condition (fast and next[fast] both exist) gives the second middle for even lengths. One pass, constant memory.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Step: slow = 3, fast = 2. Step: slow = 2, fast = -1 (after car 0).
